title: The lab page that may be lost
setup: A lab system pages the covering team about a result: the patient's potassium is high (p). In w1 it is high; in w2 it is not. Neither the nurse (N) nor the doctor (D) can tell w1 from w2 until the page arrives. Two things can happen: the page is sent (possible only where p holds), or it is lost (possible anywhere). Choose who observes what happens, then apply the update.

questions.prompt: Select D only, then apply. Click the worlds where D knows the potassium is high, but N does not know that D knows it.

hints.text: Potassium is high at both of those worlds, but at w1×lost the page never reached D, so D does not know it. Check K[D]p world by world, not p.
At least one world qualifies: D saw the page, and N cannot rule out that it was lost. Look at w1×sent.

questions.prompt: With D observing (apply it), write a formula true exactly at w1×lost: the page was lost and potassium is high.

hints.text: p is also true at w1×sent, where the page arrived. Add what separates the two: only at w1×lost does D not know p.
D also fails to know p at w2×lost, where potassium is not high. Combine it with p.

questions.prompt: Choose who observes so that D knows the potassium is high and N knows that D knows it, at w1×sent.

hints.text: D observing is not enough. N still considers the page lost as possible, and when it was lost D does not know p, so N cannot know that D knows.
N sees what happened, but D still considers the page lost as possible, so D does not yet know p.
If nobody observes, nobody learns anything from the page: both still consider lost and sent possible.

questions.prompt: Select both N and D, then apply. Click the worlds where N knows the potassium is high.

hints.text: Potassium is high at w1×lost, but N cannot rule out w2×lost there, where it is not. Knowing p needs p at every world N considers possible.
With N observing, N knows p wherever N saw the page arrive. Try w1×sent.
